newsitem.title: USA: U.S. livestock producers brace for cold, wind.
newsitem.headline: U.S. livestock producers brace for cold, wind.

text.p: U.S. livestock producers were bracing for another bout of cold weather as meteorologists predicted temperatures would drop to -10 degrees Fahrenheit in the Midwest and northern Plains later this week.
"It should be a blustery day tomorrow with light snow," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "Friday, the coldest air mass of the season will be coming to the region."
Winds up to 40 miles per hour were expected in the Dakotas and Montana on Wednesday, moving into Nebraska, Iowa and Illinois on Thursday.
"All the snow we've had is going to be horizontal in the Plains this afternoon," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express. "We'll have blowing, drifting snow."
Wind chills on Thursday were expected to drop to -55 F in Nebraska and -30 F as far south as the Texas Panhandle.
Blizzard-like conditions were expected in the Dakotas and Montana on Wednesday as heavy winds blow snow drifts and restrict visibility.
Winds should subside Friday as another round of arctic air pushes across the Plains and into the Midwest, Burgio and Gesser said.
"The focal point for the cold air seems to be from Alberta (Canada) to the Great Lakes," Gesser said.
Temperatures Friday morning were expected to sink to -10 F in Chicago. Burgio said lows in the western Corn Belt would average between -10 and -20 F Friday morning.
Meteorologists said temperatures would be somewhat warmer over the weekend but still below normal for this time of year. Long-range forecasts indicated temperatures would be near normal on Monday.
